answer: One way is to charge a real stake for each identity. An agent puts up a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers catch it running duplicate accounts. A single honest agent pays once and keeps working. An attacker running a grove of fake agents pays for every one, and each fake leaves a signal in its transaction history that peers can check. A lotus pattern helps too: new identities start with a small trust limit and earn a bigger one only after steady honest work, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot outvote established ones.
